title: Why Rioja Alavesa tastes the way it does

lede.text: Here the Atlantic and the Mediterranean meet, and the shelter of the Sierra de Cantabria counts even more than in Rioja Alta.

chapters.title: Two climates, one wall
paras: Rioja Alavesa gets about as many hours of sun as Rioja Alta and a little less rain. The Sierra de Cantabria to the north matters even more here than in Rioja Alta. Its wines have slightly more alcohol and a little less acidity than Rioja Alta's, and they are versatile: good to drink young, good to age, and good for blending.

fly.label: Sierra de Cantabria
fly.caption: The mountains on Rioja's northern side. They protect Rioja Alta, and Rioja Alavesa even more.

chapters.title: Terraces of clay-limestone
paras: Clay-limestone soils dominate, on terraces and in small plots. These are the soils the rules name as the main source of Rioja's wines for ageing. Laguardia and Elciego are among its villages.

fly.caption: Clay-limestone on terraces and small plots: the main source of Rioja's wines for ageing.
